text: The sun dipped below the horizon, casting long shadows over the quiet hamlet, when the messenger’s arrival shattered the evening’s stillness. I watched from my porch as the news spread like wildfire through the narrow streets. Neighbors who had barely spoken in years embraced, their laughter mingling with sobs. I saw old Mrs. Gable clutching her chest, her eyes wide with a disbelief that slowly melted into profound relief. The silence that had hung over our community for so long was finally broken, not by the drumbeat of war, but by the promise of return. As the crowd swelled, I looked up at the sky, wondering if the river that wound through our valley was witnessing this same moment of peace. It flows endlessly, indifferent to human strife, yet today it seemed to mirror the depth of our collective exhale. The war was done. The boys were coming home.
